chapter.name: Salient Features of the Constitution
chapter.blurb: The main features of the Indian Constitution, its sources, and the criticisms made of it.

source.title: Indian Polity (question set written from its topics)

concepts.name: Lengthiest written constitution and its sources

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about features and their sources in the chapter's table:

1. Rule of law and single citizenship are taken from the American Constitution.
2. The Concurrent List is taken from the Australian Constitution.
3. The ideal of justice in the Preamble is taken from the French Constitution.
4. Procedure established by law is taken from the Japanese Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Table 4.4 (p.82) lists both under the British Constitution. Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.4 (p.82) lists it under the Australian Constitution. Statement 3 is incorrect: Table 4.4 (p.82): the ideal of justice (social, economic and political) is from the Soviet Constitution; the French source gives liberty, equality and fraternity. Statement 4 is correct: Table 4.4 (p.82).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.82
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.82
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: In 2019 the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 was abolished by a constitutional amendment passed under Article 368.
Statement-II: The 2019 presidential order extended all the provisions of the Constitution of India to Jammu and Kashmir.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: p.63 says it was abolished by a presidential order, not an amendment. Statement-II is correct: p.63.
w: Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect, so Statement-II cannot explain Statement-I.
Rejected: it treats both as correct, but Statement-I is incorrect.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Eighth Schedule, as given in the chapter:

1. Sindhi was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Amendment Act of 1967.
2. The 92nd Amendment Act of 2003 added four languages: Bodo, Dongri, Maithili and Santhali.
3. The 96th Amendment Act of 2011 renamed Oriya as Odia.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.81. Statement 2 is correct: p.81. Statement 3 is correct: p.81. So all 3 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q: Amendments since 1951 have deleted one Part of the original Constitution. Which one of the following correctly identifies it?
questions.a: Part VII, dealing with the States in Part B, deleted by the 7th Amendment Act (1956)
o: Part VII, dealing with the States in Part B, deleted by the 7th Amendment Act (1956)
Part VIII, dealing with the Union Territories, deleted by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976)
Part XIV-A, dealing with Tribunals, deleted by the 44th Amendment Act (1978)
Part IV-A, dealing with Fundamental Duties, deleted by the 44th Amendment Act (1978)
questions.e: p.62: amendments deleted about 20 Articles and one Part (VII). p.75 note: Part VII was deleted by the 7th Amendment Act (1956).
w: Part VIII (Articles 239 to 242) still exists; it was not deleted (p.73).
Part XIV-A (Tribunals) was added, not deleted, by the 42nd Amendment (p.75).
Part IV-A was added, not deleted, by the 42nd Amendment (p.75).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the number of Articles in other Constitutions:

1. The American Constitution originally consisted of only 7 Articles.
2. The Canadian Constitution has 147 Articles.
3. The Chinese Constitution has more Articles than the Canadian.
4. The Australian Constitution has 128 Articles.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Footnote 2, p.83. Statement 2 is correct: Footnote 2, p.83. Statement 3 is incorrect: Footnote 2: Chinese 138, Canadian 147. Statement 4 is correct: Footnote 2, p.83. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).

questions.q:
With reference to the size of the Indian Constitution, consider the following statements:

1. As adopted in 1949 it contained a Preamble, 395 Articles divided into 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
2. The Constitution of India is the lengthiest of all the written Constitutions of the world.
3. The Constitution presently consists of a Preamble, about 470 Articles divided into 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.
4. No Part of the original Constitution has been deleted by any amendment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.62 gives these original numbers. Statement 2 is correct: p.62. Statement 3 is correct: p.62. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.62: one Part, Part VII, was deleted.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.62
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.62
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the contents of the Indian Constitution, according to the chapter:

1. It confines itself to the fundamental principles of governance and leaves detailed administrative provisions to ordinary legislation.
2. Matters that other modern democratic countries have left to ordinary legislation or established political conventions have also been included in the constitutional document in India.
3. No other Constitution in the world has so many Articles and Schedules.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.62: it contains not only the fundamental principles of governance but also detailed administrative provisions. Statement 2 is correct: p.62. Statement 3 is correct: p.62.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.62
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.62
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly names the Parts that were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976)?
questions.e: p.75 note: both Part IV-A and Part XIV-A were added by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976).
w: Part IX-A was added by the 74th Amendment Act (1992), not the 42nd (p.75).
Part IX-A (74th Amendment) and Part IX-B (97th Amendment) were added later (p.75).
Part IX-B was added by the 97th Amendment Act (2011) (p.75).

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the changes made in 2019 regarding the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir, as given in the chapter?
questions.a: A presidential order extended all provisions of the Constitution to it, and an Act of 2019 bifurcated it into two Union territories
o: A presidential order extended all provisions of the Constitution to it, and an Act of 2019 bifurcated it into two Union territories
A constitutional amendment passed under Article 368 repealed Article 370, and the Reorganisation Act made the whole State a single Union territory
The Reorganisation Act, 2019 divided it into two States, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, each keeping its own separate constitution
A presidential order retained the State's own constitution but placed Ladakh under the Sixth Schedule as a tribal area
questions.e: p.63: the special status under Article 370 was abolished by a presidential order, 'The Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 2019', which extended all provisions of the Constitution to it; the Reorganisation Act, 2019 created two Union territories.
w: The chapter says a presidential order, not an Article 368 amendment, was used, and two Union territories, not one, resulted (p.63).
The bifurcation was into two Union territories, not two States (p.63).
The 2019 order extended all provisions of the Constitution to the territory and ended its own constitution (p.63).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the changes made by amendments since 1951, as given in the chapter:

1. The amendments have added about 20 Articles and deleted about 95 Articles.
2. The amendments have deleted two Parts of the original Constitution.
3. The amendments have added four Parts: IVA, IXA, IXB and XIVA.
4. The amendments have added four Schedules, numbered 9, 10, 11 and 12.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.62: about 95 Articles were added and about 20 were deleted. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.62: one Part (VII) was deleted. Statement 3 is correct: p.62. Statement 4 is correct: p.62.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.62
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.62
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62

questions.q:
Match each Schedule in List-I with its subject in List-II.

List-I
A. Sixth Schedule
B. Tenth Schedule
C. Eleventh Schedule
D. Twelfth Schedule

List-II
1. Powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities
2. Disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection
3. Administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
4. Powers, authority and responsibilities of panchayats

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: pp.80-81: the Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; the Tenth covers defection; the Eleventh covers panchayats; the Twelfth covers municipalities.
w: A and B are interchanged: Sixth Schedule goes with Administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, and Tenth Schedule with Disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection.

A and D are interchanged: Sixth Schedule goes with Administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, and Twelfth Schedule with Powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities.
B and C are interchanged: Tenth Schedule goes with Disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection, and Eleventh Schedule with Powers, authority and responsibilities of panchayats.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Seventh Schedule, as given in the chapter's table (8th edition):

1. The Union List presently contains 98 subjects against 97 originally.
2. The Concurrent List presently contains fewer subjects than it originally had.
3. The State List presently contains more subjects than it originally had.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.80. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.80: 52 now against 47 originally. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.80: 59 now against 66 originally. So exactly 1 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).

questions.q: The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) is known as the 'Mini-Constitution'. According to the chapter, why is it called so?
questions.a: Because of the important and large number of changes made by it in various parts of the Constitution
o: Because of the important and large number of changes made by it in various parts of the Constitution
Because it replaced the original Preamble, Articles and Schedules with a freshly drafted shorter text
Because it brought the Constitution back to the size it had when it was adopted in 1949
Because it deleted the Right to Property from Part III and added the Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: p.62: the 42nd Amendment Act (1976) is known as the 'Mini-Constitution' due to the important and large number of changes made by it in various parts of the Constitution.
w: It changed parts of the existing text; it did not replace the whole document with a shorter one (p.62).
It made changes in various parts of the Constitution; it did not reduce it to its 1949 size (p.62).
The Right to Property was deleted by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978, and the Directive Principles were in the original Constitution (p.66).

questions.q: Four factors are cited for the elephantine size of the Indian Constitution. Which one of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.a: The influence of the American Constitution
o: The influence of the American Constitution
The vastness of the country and its diversity
The influence of the Government of India Act of 1935, which was bulky
The dominance of legal luminaries in the Constituent Assembly
questions.e: p.62 gives geographical, historical (1935 Act), single Constitution for Centre and states, and legal luminaries as the four factors. The American Constitution is not among them; footnote 2 (p.83) says it originally had only 7 Articles.
w: This is the geographical factor named on p.62.
This is the historical factor named on p.62.
This is the fourth factor named on p.62.

questions.q:
According to the chapter, consider the following statements about the Ninth Schedule and the case linked to it:

1. The Ninth Schedule originally contained 13 Acts and Regulations.
2. The Ninth Schedule presently contains 284 Acts and Regulations.
3. Laws included in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review.
4. 24 April 1973 is the date on which the Supreme Court delivered its judgement in Kesavananda Bharati.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.81. Statement 2 is incorrect: Footnote 25 (p.84): the last entry is numbered 284 but the actual total is 282. Statement 3 is correct: p.81. Statement 4 is correct: Footnote 26 (p.84).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.81
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.81
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.81

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A number of the original features of the Constitution (as adopted in 1949) have undergone a substantial change.
Statement-II: Several amendments, particularly the 7th, 42nd, 44th, 73rd, 74th, 97th and 101st, have been made to the Constitution.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.62. Statement-II is correct: p.62 names these amendments. Statement-II explains Statement-I: p.62 says the original features have undergone a substantial change 'on account of several amendments, particularly' these.
w: Rejected: the chapter itself attributes the change to these amendments, so Statement-II does explain Statement-I (p.62).
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but the chapter names exactly these amendments (p.62).
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but the chapter says original features have substantially changed (p.62).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the opening remarks of the chapter:

1. The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) is known as the 'Mini-Constitution'.
2. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament's power under Article 368 enables it to alter even the basic structure.
3. The 7th, 42nd, 44th, 73rd, 74th, 97th and 101st Amendments are cited as having substantially changed original features.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.62. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.62: the Court ruled that the power does not enable it to alter the basic structure. Statement 3 is correct: p.62.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.62
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the factors behind the size of the Indian Constitution:

1. The vastness and diversity of the country is a historical factor.
2. The bulky Government of India Act of 1935 influenced the Constitution, a historical factor.
3. A single Constitution for both the Centre and the states added to its length.
4. The dominance of legal luminaries in the Constituent Assembly contributed to its size.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.62 names it as the geographical factor. Statement 2 is correct: p.62. Statement 3 is correct: p.62. Statement 4 is correct: p.62.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.62
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935 as a source:

1. The federal scheme, judiciary, governors, emergency powers and Public Service Commissions are drawn from it.
2. More than half of the provisions of the Constitution are identical to or closely resemble the Act of 1935.
3. The Fundamental Duties are traced to the Act of 1935.
4. The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is a feature borrowed from the 1935 Act.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.63. Statement 2 is correct: p.63. Statement 3 is incorrect: Table 4.4 (p.82) traces the Fundamental Duties to the Soviet Constitution. Statement 4 is correct: Table 4.4 (p.81).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.63
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.63
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.63

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sources of the Indian Constitution, according to the chapter:

1. Provisions have been drawn from the Constitutions of Canada, Australia and Germany but not from those of France, South Africa or Japan.
2. The Constitution has borrowed most of its provisions from the Government of India Act of 1935 and none from other countries.
3. According to the footnote, about 250 provisions of the 1935 Act have been included in the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.63 lists Canada, Australia, Germany, USSR (now Russia), France, South Africa and Japan. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.63: most provisions are borrowed from the Constitutions of various other countries as well as from the 1935 Act. Statement 3 is correct: footnote 3, p.83.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.63
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.63
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.63

concepts.name: Rigidity with flexibility and a federal system with a unitary bias

questions.q:
With reference to the amendment of the Indian Constitution, consider the following statements:

1. The Constitution of India is a flexible Constitution, like the British Constitution.
2. A rigid Constitution requires a special procedure for its amendment, as in the American Constitution.
3. A flexible Constitution can be amended in the manner of ordinary laws, as in the British Constitution.
4. Some provisions of the Indian Constitution can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament, and such amendments do not come under Article 368.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.63: it is neither rigid nor flexible but a synthesis of both. Statement 2 is correct: p.63. Statement 3 is correct: p.63. Statement 4 is correct: p.64.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.63
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.63
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.63

questions.q: Amendments of certain provisions of the Constitution are made by a simple majority of Parliament in the manner of ordinary legislation. Which one of the following is correct about such amendments?
questions.a: They do not come under Article 368
o: They do not come under Article 368
They require ratification by half of the total states
They require a two-third majority of members present and voting in each House
They are made under Article 368 by a special majority
questions.e: p.64: some provisions can be amended by a simple majority in the manner of ordinary legislative process, and 'notably, these amendments do not come under Article 368'.
w: Ratification by half the states applies only to the second type of Article 368 amendment (p.64).
A two-third majority present and voting is the special majority, not the simple one (p.63).
Article 368 deals with the two special-majority types only (p.63-64).

questions.q: The description of the Indian Constitution as a 'federation with a centralising tendency' is associated with
questions.e: p.64: Wheare - quasi-federal; Morris Jones - bargaining federalism; Granville Austin - co-operative federalism; Ivor Jennings - federation with a centralising tendency.
w: Wheare called it 'quasi-federal'.
Morris Jones called it 'bargaining federalism'.
Granville Austin called it 'co-operative federalism'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the chapter's table of important Articles:

1. Article 249 deals with the power of Parliament to legislate with respect to a matter in the State List in the national interest.
2. Article 263 deals with provisions with respect to an inter-state council.
3. Article 155 deals with the power of the governor to promulgate ordinances.
4. Article 169 deals with the appointment of the governor.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.77). Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.77). Statement 3 is incorrect: Table 4.2 (p.77): Article 155 is appointment of the governor; Article 213 is the ordinance power. Statement 4 is incorrect: Table 4.2 (p.77): Article 169 is abolition or creation of legislative councils in states.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.77
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.77
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.77

questions.q: Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States'. Which one of the following is an implication stated in the chapter?
questions.a: No state has the right to secede from the federation
o: No state has the right to secede from the federation
The Indian federation is the result of an agreement among the states
The word 'Federation' is used in the Constitution as a synonym for the Union
States may leave the Union with the consent of Parliament
questions.e: p.64: the phrase implies two things: the federation is not the result of an agreement by the states, and no state has the right to secede.
w: The chapter says the opposite: it is not the result of an agreement (p.64).
The chapter says the term 'Federation' has nowhere been used (p.64).
No state has a right to secede; the chapter does not mention any consent route (p.64).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Constitution of India is a synthesis of rigidity and flexibility.
Statement-II: Bicameralism is among the usual features of a federation that the Indian Constitution contains.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.63. Statement-II is correct: p.64 lists it among the federal features; it is a separate fact and does not account for the blend of amendment procedures. Statement-II concerns the federal system, not the amendment procedures.
w: Rejected: both are correct but Statement-II only states a separate fact; it does not give the reason for Statement-I.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the classification of Constitutions:

1. The American Constitution is an example of an unwritten Constitution.
2. The British Constitution is an example of a written Constitution.
3. The American Constitution is an example of a rigid Constitution.
4. The British Constitution is an example of a rigid Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.62: the American Constitution is written. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.62: the British Constitution is unwritten. Statement 3 is correct: p.63. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.63: the British Constitution is flexible.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.62
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.62

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The term 'Federation' has been used in Article 1 to describe India.
Statement-II: Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States'.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: p.64: the term 'Federation' has nowhere been used in the Constitution. Statement-II is correct: p.64.
w: Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect, so Statement-II cannot explain Statement-I.
Rejected: it treats both as correct, but Statement-I is incorrect.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Canadian Constitution as a source:

1. A federation with a strong Centre is taken from it.
2. Vesting of residuary powers in the Centre is taken from it.
3. Appointment of state governors by the Centre is taken from it.
4. The Concurrent List is taken from it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 4.4 (p.82). Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.4 (p.82). Statement 3 is correct: Table 4.4 (p.82). Statement 4 is incorrect: Table 4.4 (p.82): the Concurrent List is from the Australian Constitution.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.82
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.82
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about citizenship and the federal system:

1. A single citizenship is listed among the federal features of the Indian Constitution.
2. In the USA each person is a citizen of the nation and also of the particular state to which he belongs.
3. In India the citizens of different states enjoy different sets of civil rights according to the state of their birth.
4. India has a dual polity but provides for only one citizenship.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.64 lists single citizenship among the unitary or non-federal features. Statement 2 is correct: p.68. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.68: all citizens enjoy the same political and civil rights all over the country. Statement 4 is correct: p.68.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.64
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.64
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.64

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about emergencies and the federal structure:

1. During an emergency the federal structure is converted into a unitary one without a formal amendment of the Constitution.
2. This transformation is described as a unique feature of the Indian Constitution.
3. The Central Government becomes all-powerful during a National Emergency but not during President's Rule.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.69. Statement 2 is correct: p.69. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.69: the Central Government becomes all-powerful during an emergency, and the chapter lists President's Rule among the three types. So exactly 2 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 2).

questions.q: A special majority of Parliament under Article 368 means
questions.a: two-third of the members of each House present and voting, and a majority of the total membership of each House
o: two-third of the members of each House present and voting, and a majority of the total membership of each House
two-third of the total membership of each House
a majority of the members present and voting in each House with ratification by half of the states
three-fourth of the members present and voting in each House
questions.e: p.63: a two-third majority of the members of each House present and voting, and a majority of the total membership of each House.
w: Two-thirds applies to members present and voting, not the total membership (p.63).
That describes a simple majority plus ratification, which is not the special majority (p.63-64).
Three-fourth is not the figure given for Parliament (p.63).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the federal features of the Indian Constitution:

1. Division of powers between the Centre and the states is a federal feature.
2. An independent judiciary is a federal feature.
3. Supremacy of the Constitution is a federal feature.
4. Bicameralism is a federal feature.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.64. Statement 2 is correct: p.64. Statement 3 is correct: p.64. Statement 4 is correct: p.64 lists it among the usual features of a federation.

1. Article 17 deals with the abolition of untouchability.
2. Article 21A deals with the right to elementary education.
3. Article 50 deals with the separation of the judiciary from the executive.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.75). Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.75). Statement 3 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.76). So all 3 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the nature of Fundamental Rights:

1. An aggrieved person must first approach the High Court and cannot go directly to the Supreme Court.
2. They are justiciable, that is, enforceable by courts for their violation.
3. They are not absolute and are subject to reasonable restrictions.
4. They cannot be curtailed or repealed by Parliament through a Constitutional Amendment Act.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.66: he can directly go to the Supreme Court. Statement 2 is correct: p.66. Statement 3 is correct: p.66. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.66: they can be curtailed or repealed by a Constitutional Amendment Act.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.66
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.66
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.66

questions.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy can be classified into three broad categories. Which one of the following is that classification?
questions.e: p.66: socialistic, Gandhian and liberal-intellectual.
w: Political, social and economic are kinds of democracy, not categories of directives.
Not a classification used in the chapter.
'Marxist' is not a category; the third is liberal-intellectual (p.66).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Fundamental Rights are sacrosanct and cannot be curtailed by a Constitutional Amendment Act.
Statement-II: The Fundamental Rights are not absolute and are subject to reasonable restrictions.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
o: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect: p.66 says they can be curtailed or repealed by a Constitutional Amendment Act. Statement-II is correct: p.66.
w: Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect, so Statement-II cannot explain Statement-I.
Rejected: it treats both as correct, but Statement-I is incorrect.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Directive Principles of State Policy:

1. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described them as a 'novel feature' of the Constitution.
2. They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution.
3. They are meant for promoting the ideal of political democracy.
4. They seek to establish a 'welfare state' in India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.66. Statement 2 is correct: p.66. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.66: they promote social and economic democracy; Fundamental Rights promote political democracy. Statement 4 is correct: p.66.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.66
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.66
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.66

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Although the Directive Principles are non-justiciable, they impose a moral obligation on the state authorities.
Statement-II: The Constitution itself declares that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and that it shall be the duty of the state to apply them in making laws.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.66. Statement-II is correct: p.66; this declaration is the basis of the moral obligation.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is the reason for Statement-I here, so it does explain it.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Directive Principles form a part of Part III of the Constitution.
2. The Fundamental Duties are enforceable by the courts.
3. Part IV-A of the Constitution consists of several Articles dealing with the duties of citizens.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.66: they are in Part IV. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.67: they are non-justiciable. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.66: Part IV-A consists of only one Article, 51-A. So none is correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: none of the statements is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: none of the statements is correct.
'All three' miscounts: none of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Duties:

1. Part IV-A consists of only one Article, 51-A.
2. The Fundamental Duties were added during the operation of the internal emergency of 1975-77.
3. Like the Directive Principles, the duties are non-justiciable.
4. The original Constitution provided for the Fundamental Duties of the citizens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.66. Statement 2 is correct: p.66. Statement 3 is correct: p.67. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.66: it did not.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.66
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.66
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.66

questions.q:
With reference to the secular character of the State, consider the following statements:

1. The term 'secular' was added to the Preamble by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
2. Article 27 says that no person shall be compelled to pay any taxes for the promotion of a particular religion.
3. Article 29 gives all minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
4. Article 44 asks the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.67: by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976. Statement 2 is correct: p.67. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.67: that is Article 30; Article 29 protects the right to conserve distinct language, script or culture. Statement 4 is correct: p.67.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.67
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.67
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.67

questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution during the internal emergency of 1975-77. Which one of the following correctly states how?
questions.a: By the 42nd Amendment Act (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee
o: By the 42nd Amendment Act (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee
By the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee
By the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission
By the 86th Amendment Act of 2002 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee
questions.e: p.66: added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee; the 86th Amendment of 2002 added one more.
w: The 44th Amendment deleted the right to property; it did not add duties (p.66).
The chapter names the Swaran Singh Committee as the recommending body (p.66).
The 86th Amendment added only one more duty, not the duties as such (p.66).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Parts of the Constitution in the chapter's table:

1. Part III (Fundamental Rights) covers Articles 12 to 25.
2. Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) covers Articles 36 to 51.
3. Part IX deals with the Municipalities.
4. Part IV-A (Fundamental Duties) covers Article 51-A.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Table 4.1 (p.72): Articles 12 to 35. Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.1 (p.72). Statement 3 is incorrect: Table 4.1 (p.73): Part IX is the Panchayats; Part IX-A is the Municipalities. Statement 4 is correct: Table 4.1 (p.72).
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.72
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.72
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.72

concepts.name: Adult franchise, single citizenship, independent bodies, emergency provisions, three-tier and co-operative government

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about panchayats and municipalities:

1. Part IX-A of the Constitution deals with the panchayats.
2. The municipal corporation is provided for a transitional area.
3. The nagar panchayat is provided for a transitional area.
4. The municipal council is provided for a smaller urban area.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.69: Part IX deals with panchayats; Part IX-A with municipalities. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.69: it is for a larger urban area. Statement 3 is correct: p.69. Statement 4 is correct: p.69.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.69
'3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.69
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.69

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about independent bodies:

1. A State Public Service Commission advises the President on disciplinary matters.
2. The Election Commission ensures free and fair elections to Parliament, the state legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.
3. The Comptroller and Auditor-General audits the accounts of the Central Government but not of the state governments.
4. The UPSC conducts examinations for All-India services and higher Central services.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.68: it advises the governor. Statement 2 is correct: p.68. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.68: he audits the accounts of the Central and state governments. Statement 4 is correct: p.68.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.68
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.68
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.68

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly pairs a type of municipality with the area for which it is provided, as given in the chapter?
questions.a: Municipal council - a smaller urban area
o: Municipal council - a smaller urban area
Nagar panchayat - a larger urban area
Municipal council - a larger urban area
questions.e: p.69: nagar panchayat for a transitional area, municipal council for a smaller urban area, municipal corporation for a larger urban area.
w: A nagar panchayat is for a transitional area (p.69).
A municipal corporation is for a larger urban area (p.69).
A municipal council is for a smaller urban area (p.69).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. India has a single citizenship.
2. Each Indian citizen owes allegiance to both the Centre and his state.
3. The UPSC advises the President on disciplinary matters of civil servants.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.68. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.68: this is the position in the USA, not India. Statement 3 is correct: p.68. So exactly 2 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The introduction of universal adult franchise by the Constitution-makers was a bold experiment and highly remarkable.
Statement-II: At that time the country had a vast size, a huge population, high poverty, social inequality and overwhelming illiteracy.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.68. Statement-II is correct: p.68 states the experiment was remarkable 'in view of' these conditions.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is the reason for Statement-I here, so it does explain it.
Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q: According to the chapter, which Article is linked with the ground of failure to comply with the directions of the Centre for a state emergency (President's Rule)?
questions.e: p.69 and Table 4.2 (p.78): a state emergency arises on the ground of failure of constitutional machinery in the states (Article 356) or failure to comply with the directions of the Centre (Article 365).
w: Article 352 is the national emergency on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion (p.69).
Article 356 is linked in the chapter with the separate ground of failure of constitutional machinery (p.69).
Article 360 is the financial emergency (p.69).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the third tier of government:

1. The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts (1992) added a third tier of government.
2. A third tier of government is found in all federal Constitutions of the world.
3. The 73rd Amendment Act added a new Part IX and Schedule 11.
4. The 74th Amendment Act added a new Part IX-A and Schedule 12.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.69. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.69: it is not found in any other Constitution of the world. Statement 3 is correct: p.69. Statement 4 is correct: p.69.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.69
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.69
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.69

questions.q:
Match each Article in List-I with the subject it deals with in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 352
B. Article 356
C. Article 360
D. Article 365

List-II
1. Threat to the financial stability or credit of India
2. War, external aggression or armed rebellion
3. Failure of constitutional machinery in the states
4. Failure to comply with directions given by the Union

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
w: A and D are interchanged: Article 352 goes with War, external aggression or armed rebellion, and Article 365 with Failure to comply with directions given by the Union.
A and B are interchanged: Article 352 goes with War, external aggression or armed rebellion, and Article 356 with Failure of constitutional machinery in the states.
A and C are interchanged: Article 352 goes with War, external aggression or armed rebellion, and Article 360 with Threat to the financial stability or credit of India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the extension of the franchise to women, as given in the chapter's footnote:

1. Switzerland gave the franchise to women in 1948.
2. The USA gave the franchise to women in 1920.
3. Britain gave the franchise to women in 1928.
4. France gave the franchise to women in 1945.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Footnote 10, p.83: Switzerland in 1971; 1948 is the year given for Italy. Statement 2 is correct: Footnote 10, p.83. Statement 3 is correct: Footnote 10, p.83. Statement 4 is correct: Footnote 10, p.83.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.83
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.83
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.83

questions.q:
With reference to universal adult franchise, consider the following statements:

1. It is the basis of elections to the Lok Sabha and the state legislative assemblies.
2. A citizen not less than 18 years of age has a right to vote without discrimination of caste, race, religion, sex, literacy or wealth.
3. The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
4. Universal adult franchise makes democracy broad-based and enhances the self-respect and prestige of the common people.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.68. Statement 2 is correct: p.68. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.68: by the 61st Amendment Act of 1988. Statement 4 is correct: p.68.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.68
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.68
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.68

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the chapter's table of important Articles:

1. Article 315 deals with Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the states.
2. Article 320 deals with the functions of Public Service Commissions.
3. Article 324 deals with superintendence, direction and control of elections vested in an Election Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.78). Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.78). Statement 3 is correct: Table 4.2 (p.78).
w: '1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.78
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.78
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.78

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts added a third tier of government which is not found in any other Constitution of the world.
Statement-II: The 74th Amendment Act added a new Part IX and a new Schedule 11 to give constitutional recognition to municipalities.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.69. Statement-II is incorrect: p.69: Part IX-A and Schedule 12 were added for municipalities; Part IX and Schedule 11 were for panchayats.
w: Rejected: one of the two statements is incorrect, so Statement-II cannot explain Statement-I.
Rejected: it treats both as correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q: According to the chapter, which one of the following is NOT a change made by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 relating to co-operative societies?
questions.a: Adding a new Schedule dealing with co-operative societies
o: Adding a new Schedule dealing with co-operative societies
Making the right to form co-operative societies a fundamental right under Article 19
Including a new Directive Principle on promotion of co-operative societies in Article 43-B
Adding a new Part IX-B entitled 'The Co-operative Societies'
questions.e: pp.69-70: three changes - Article 19, Article 43-B, and Part IX-B (Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT). No Schedule was added by it. Currency note: the question follows the chapter; in Union of India v. Rajendra Shah (2021) the Supreme Court struck down Part IX-B as it applies to co-operative societies in the states, leaving it effective for multi-state co-operative societies.
w: One of the three changes (p.69).
One of the three changes (p.69).
One of the three changes (p.70).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about citizenship:

1. India provides for a single citizenship despite being federal with a dual polity.
2. In the USA, a person is a citizen of the nation and not of the state.
3. In India all citizens enjoy the same political and civil rights irrespective of the state in which they are born or reside.
4. The goal of building a united and integrated Indian nation has been fully realised.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.68. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.68: he is a citizen of the nation and of the particular state. Statement 3 is correct: p.68. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.68: it has not been fully realised.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.68
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.68
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.68

questions.q: The 73rd Amendment Act provides for a three-tier system of panchayati raj in every state. At which levels are the panchayats constituted?
o: Village, block, district and national levels
questions.e: p.69: panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels.
w: The chapter names three levels, not four, and none is national (p.69).
Municipalities are the urban local bodies under Part IX-A; panchayats are rural (p.69).
The chapter's third level is the district, not the state (p.69).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the effect of an emergency:

1. During an emergency the states retain their full control over their subjects.
2. The federal structure is converted into a unitary one through a formal amendment under Article 368.
3. This transformation from federal to unitary is described as a unique feature of the Indian Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.69: the states go into the total control of the Centre. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.69: the conversion takes place without a formal amendment of the Constitution. Statement 3 is correct: p.69.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.69
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.69
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.69

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the chapter's table of Parts and Articles:

1. The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is dealt with in Articles 148 to 151 (Part V, Chapter V).
2. Public Service Commissions are dealt with in Articles 315 to 323 (Part XIV, Chapter II).
3. Part XV of the Constitution deals with Elections.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 4.1 (p.72). Statement 2 is correct: Table 4.1 (p.74). Statement 3 is correct: Table 4.1 (p.74). So all 3 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q:
According to the chapter, consider the following statements about the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011:

1. It was passed in 2002.
2. It made the right to form co-operative societies a fundamental right under Article 19.
3. It included a Directive Principle on promotion of co-operative societies in Article 43-B.
4. Its Part IX-B empowers Parliament to make law for all co-operative societies.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.69: the Act is of 2011; 2002 is the year of the 86th Amendment. Statement 2 is correct: p.69. Statement 3 is correct: p.69. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.70: Parliament for multi-state societies; state legislatures for the others. Currency note: in Union of India v. Rajendra Shah (2021) the Supreme Court struck down Part IX-B as it applies to co-operative societies in the states, so statement 4 is judged here on the chapter's text.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.69
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.69
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.69

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about All-India services, as given in the footnote:

1. At present there are four All-India services: the IAS, IPS, IFoS and the Indian Civil Service.
2. In 1947 the Indian Civil Service was replaced by the IAS.
3. The Indian Forest Service came into existence in 1966.
4. The Indian Police was replaced by the IPS in 1966.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Footnote 11, p.83: three - IAS, IPS and IFoS. Statement 2 is correct: Footnote 11, p.83. Statement 3 is correct: Footnote 11, p.83. Statement 4 is incorrect: Footnote 11: it was replaced in 1947; 1966 is when IFoS began. So exactly 2 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 2, 3).
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 2, 3).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 2, 3).

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the independent bodies listed in the chapter as being established by the Constitution?
questions.e: p.68 lists four: Election Commission, CAG, UPSC and State Public Service Commissions. The Attorney-General is not listed.
w: Listed first on p.68.
Listed second on p.68.
Listed third on p.68.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'carbon copy' criticism:

1. K. Hanumanthaiya said the Constitution is essentially the 1935 Act with only adult franchise added.
2. N. Srinivasan observed that the Constitution is a close copy of the Act of 1935 in language and substance.
3. Sir Ivor Jennings said the Constitution derives directly from the Government of India Act of 1919.
4. Ambedkar said there was nothing to be ashamed of in borrowing.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.70: this was P.R. Deshmukh. Statement 2 is correct: p.70. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.70: he said it derives directly from the Act of 1935. Statement 4 is correct: p.70.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.70
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.70
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.70

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'un-Indian' criticism:

1. It claims that the Constitution reflects the political traditions of India.
2. Lokanath Misra called it a 'slavish imitation of the west'.
3. Lakshminarayan Sahu said the Constitution would prove suitable and endure.
4. The critics said the foreign nature of the Constitution makes it unsuitable or unworkable in India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.71: it claims the Constitution does not reflect them. Statement 2 is correct: p.71. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.71: he said it would not prove suitable and would break down soon. Statement 4 is correct: p.71.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.71
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.71
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.71

questions.q: Which criticism of the Constitution holds that its legal language and phraseology make it a complex document?
questions.e: p.71: under 'Paradise of the Lawyers' the critics said the Constitution is too legalistic and very complicated, its legal language making it a complex document.
w: That criticism is about the large number of 1935 Act provisions (p.70).
That criticism is about the lack of originality (p.70).
That criticism is about the absence of Gandhi's ideals and village panchayats (p.71).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the labels used for criticisms:

1. 'Paradise of the Lawyers' is the label used for the un-Gandhian criticism.
2. 'Amended Version of the 1935 Act' is a label used under the 'carbon copy' criticism.
3. 'Hotch-potch' and 'patchwork' are used under the criticism that the Constitution is borrowed.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.71: it is a separate criticism, about legalistic complexity. Statement 2 is correct: p.70. Statement 3 is correct: p.70.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.71
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.71
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.71

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Sir Ivor Jennings called the Constitution a 'lawyer's paradise'.
2. H.K. Maheswari said the draft would make people more truthful and more likely to follow the methods of truth and non-violence.
3. Sir Ivor Jennings observed that the provisions borrowed were well selected and the Constitution was of a convenient length.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.71. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.71: he said it would make people less truthful and less likely to follow those methods. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.71: he said they were not always well-selected and the Constitution was too long and complicated. So exactly 1 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's reply that Constitutions look similar:

1. He said that fewer than fifty years had rolled over since the first written Constitution was drafted.
2. He said the fundamentals of a Constitution are recognised all over the world.
3. He said all Constitutions in their main provisions must look similar.
4. He said what the scope of a Constitution should be is still unsettled.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.70: more than hundred years. Statement 2 is correct: p.70. Statement 3 is correct: p.70. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.70: he said it has long been settled.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.70
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.70
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.70

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's reply on the 1935 Act:

1. He said he offered his apologies for reproducing a good part of the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935.
2. He said nobody holds any patent rights in the fundamental ideas of a Constitution.
3. He said borrowing involves no plagiarism.
4. He said there is nothing to be ashamed of in borrowing.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.70: 'I make no apologies'. Statement 2 is correct: p.70. Statement 3 is correct: p.70. Statement 4 is correct: p.70.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.70

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the remarks of P.R. Deshmukh on the draft:

1. He said the draft seemed to him far too ponderous, like the ponderous tomes of a law manual.
2. He said a constitutional document should use a great deal of padding and verbiage.
3. He described the draft as a vibrating, pulsating and life-giving document.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.72. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.72: he said a document dealing with a constitution hardly uses so much padding and verbiage. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.72: he said it should have been one, but 'that was not to be'. So exactly 1 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statement 1).

questions.q:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The chapter describes the criticism that the Constitution is a 'borrowed Constitution' as unfair and illogical.
Statement-II: The framers of the Constitution made necessary modifications in the features borrowed from other constitutions for their suitability to Indian conditions, at the same time avoiding their faults.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

Rejected: it calls Statement-II incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: it calls Statement-I incorrect, but Statement-I is correct.

questions.q: Who attributed the Constitution's lapse of not being built on village and district panchayats to Ambedkar's non-participation in the Gandhian movement and antagonism towards Gandhian ideas?
questions.e: p.71: T. Prakasam, another member of the Constituent Assembly, attributed this lapse to Ambedkar's non-participation and antagonism. Hanumanthaiya made the remark about what Gandhi did not want.
w: Hanumanthaiya said it was exactly the kind of Constitution Gandhi did not want (p.71).
Misra called it a slavish imitation of the west (p.71).
Sahu said it had no manifest relation to the spirit of India (p.71).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'un-Gandhian' criticism:

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.71. Statement 2 is correct: p.71. Statement 3 is correct: p.71. Statement 4 is correct: p.71.

'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.71

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the criticisms of size and complexity:

1. H.K. Maheswari said the draft would make people less litigious.
2. Sir Ivor Jennings observed that the provisions borrowed were not always well selected and the Constitution was too long and complicated.
3. H.V. Kamath linked the elephant emblem of the Assembly with the bulk of the Constitution.
4. H.V. Kamath said he was sure the House agreed that the Constitution should be made an elephantine one.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.71: he said it would make people more litigious. Statement 2 is correct: p.71. Statement 3 is correct: p.71. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.71: he said he was sure the House does not agree.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the grounds of criticism listed in the chapter:

1. 'Elephantine size' is one of the grounds of criticism.
2. 'Paradise of the lawyers' is one of the grounds of criticism.
3. 'Too brief and lacking in detail' is one of the grounds of criticism.
4. 'Un-Indian or anti-Indian' is one of the grounds of criticism.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.71. Statement 2 is correct: p.71. Statement 3 is incorrect: pp.70-71: the six grounds are borrowed, carbon copy of the 1935 Act, un-Indian, un-Gandhian, elephantine size and paradise of lawyers. Statement 4 is correct: p.71. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).

questions.q: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said he was sorry about one aspect of the provisions of the Constitution taken from the Government of India Act, 1935. What was it?
questions.a: They relate mostly to the details of administration
o: They relate mostly to the details of administration
They reproduce a federal scheme that he considered unsuitable for India
They relate mostly to the fundamental rights of the citizens
They amount to plagiarism of the Act
questions.e: pp.70-71: 'What I am sorry about is that the provisions taken from the Government of India Act, 1935, relate mostly to the details of administration.' He said borrowing involves no plagiarism.
w: He did not call the federal scheme unsuitable; he said he made no apologies for the borrowing (pp.70-71).
He said they relate mostly to details of administration, not to fundamental rights (p.71).
He said borrowing involves no plagiarism (p.70).

questions.q: Which member of the Constituent Assembly observed that the draft Constitution 'would not prove suitable and would break down soon after being brought into operation'?
questions.e: p.71: Lakshminarayan Sahu, another member of the Constituent Assembly, made this observation.
w: Misra called it a 'slavish imitation of the west' (p.71).
Hanumanthaiya spoke of the music of an English band instead of Veena or Sitar (p.71).
Maheswari called the draft a lawyer's paradise (p.71).

questions.q:

questions.q: Which one of the following criticisms is NOT attributed to Sir Ivor Jennings in the chapter?
o: That the Constitution is a carbon copy of the Act of 1935
That the Constitution is too long and complicated
That the Constitution is a lawyer's paradise
questions.e: pp.70-71: Jennings said the Constitution derives directly from the 1935 Act, that it was too long and complicated, and called it a 'lawyer's paradise'. The un-Gandhian charge is made by Hanumanthaiya and Prakasam.
w: Jennings is quoted on this on p.70.
Jennings is quoted on this on p.71.
Jennings called it a 'lawyer's paradise' on p.71.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The 'un-Gandhian' criticism holds that the Constitution should have been raised and built upon village panchayats and district panchayats.
Statement-II: The 73rd Amendment Act of 1992 gave constitutional recognition to the panchayats by adding a new Part IX-A and a new Schedule 12.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
